messages:
leo: Hey everyone, first day here! On mac M1, using Homebrew + asdf + pyenv accidentally (old dotfiles). Running into two small things: 1) python from asdf isn't being used (system python wins), and 2) my VS Code integrated terminal doesn't see the asdf shims until I restart the window. Any quick fixes?

mina: welcome :wave: For python prefer one manager — either asdf or pyenv. If keeping asdf, remove pyenv from PATH and uninstall pyenv, or configure `ASDF_PYTHON_EXE` to point to the right binary. Also ensure `~/.asdf/shims` is at the front of PATH.

leo: how do you ensure shims are first? My .zshrc appends them but old brew paths are earlier.

mina: prepend instead of append: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` in ~/.zprofile (login shells) and ~/.zshrc (interactive). On mac, also check /etc/paths files.

leo: VS Code issue: I tried adding the same export to ~/.zprofile but terminal still uses old PATH until I restart. Any settings to avoid restarting?

carmen: set the workspace setting `"terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx": ["-l"]` so the terminal launches as a login shell and sources zprofile. Also if you use the VS Code status bar command "Reload Window" it picks up changes without full quit.

leo: awesome, thanks. One more: dotfiles install uses GNU stow and moves a legacy pyenv config into PATH; should I edit the dotfiles before stowing?

mina: yes edit the dotfiles repo (we keep `dotfiles/mac/` overrides). Add a conditional to your install script to skip pyenv lines for M1: `if [ "$(uname -m)" = "arm64" ]; then skip_pyenv=true; fi`. We have a PR template for dotfile changes in the repo, ping me and I can review.

infra-bot: Reminder: mark "dev env configured" on your onboarding checklist: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/12345

leo: done, added myself to #dev-experience. Appreciate the help! :grin:
